result.topic_en: Numerical examples for water flowing through a long aqueduct with friction, showing how much of the jet height friction consumes for pipes of different widths.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM 377

101. Casus prior potissimum inseruit retardationi aquae per aquaeductus a frictione ortae determinandae. Cuius motus, vt exemplum exhibeamus, sit altitudo aquae in receptaculo $a$ valde parua, longitudo aquaeductus $BE = b = 2000$ ped. amplitudo $gg = \frac{16}{25}$, seu $g = \frac{4}{5}$ ped. altitudo $bc$, seu $b\cos.\zeta = 150$ ped. foramen autem $kk$ tam paruum, vt $\frac{k^4}{g^4}$ pro nihilo haberi possit. Denique sit tubuli $CD$ altitudo $c = \frac{1}{10}$ [?] ped. et $h = \frac{1}{100}$ [?] ped.

102. His positis sumto $\alpha = \frac{1}{4000}$ erit $\frac{\alpha b}{g} = \frac{5}{8}$, ideoque $e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} = 0,535255$ et $e^{\frac{\alpha c}{h}} = 1,002503$. Hinc ergo erit
$v = \frac{3}{2}$ [?] $a + 97,42124$ pedum.
Hoc ergo casu, dummodo fuerit altitudo vasis $AB$ sex pedum, aqua per lumen $DD$ exsiliet ad altitudinem 100 pedum, sicque frictio 50 pedes a iactu absumit.

103. Si reliquis manentibus iisdem, sit $gg = 1$ et $g = 1$, erit $\frac{\alpha b}{g} = \frac{1}{2}$ et $e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} = 0,606531$, hincque reperitur
$v = \frac{5}{5}$ [?] $a + 106,24$ pedum,
ita vt aqua ad nouem pedes altius sit ascensura, quam casu praecedente, ob auctam tubi $BE$ amplitudinem. Sin autem amplitudo tubi diminuatur, vt sit $gg = \frac{9}{25}$, seu $g = \frac{3}{5}$ ped. ob $\frac{\alpha b}{g} = \frac{5}{6}$ erit $e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} = 0,43460$, ideoque altitudo celeritati effluxus debita

Tom.VI.Nou.Com. Bbb $v = \frac{5}{7}$ [?]

items.quote: Hoc ergo casu, dummodo fuerit altitudo vasis $AB$ sex pedum, aqua per lumen $DD$ exsiliet ad altitudinem 100 pedum, sicque frictio 50 pedes a iactu absumit.
items.english: In this case, provided the height of the vessel AB is six feet, the water will spring through the opening DD to a height of 100 feet, and so friction takes 50 feet away from the jet.

items.quote: ita vt aqua ad nouem pedes altius sit ascensura, quam casu praecedente, ob auctam tubi $BE$ amplitudinem.
items.english: So the water will rise about nine feet higher than in the preceding case, because the width of the pipe BE has been increased.

items.quote: Sin autem amplitudo tubi diminuatur, vt sit $gg = \frac{9}{25}$, seu $g = \frac{3}{5}$ ped. ob $\frac{\alpha b}{g} = \frac{5}{6}$ erit $e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} = 0,43460$, ideoque altitudo celeritati effluxus debita
items.english: But if the width of the pipe is reduced, so that gg = 9/25, or g = 3/5 ft, then since αb/g = 5/6 we have e^{-αb/g} = 0.43460, and hence the height corresponding to the outflow velocity [is]...
